methodology.method: Same systematic stratified sample as Phase 8 (every 7th row by id from the id-sorted 2535-record dataset, ~stratified across response-length terciles). Each sampled row's context_raw + response_raw read and classified for self-deprecation using a fixed definition applied before classification began.

placement: whole (entire response is a single self-deprecating beat -- typical given short 1-2 sentence response length)

methodology.definition_self_deprecation: A response is coded self-deprecating only if Chandler explicitly frames something about HIMSELF (his competence, appearance, past behavior, courage, relationship, or intelligence) in a self-critical or self-mocking way. Absurdist non-sequiturs, deflecting compliments with unrelated jokes that are not self-critical, and general sarcasm not aimed at self were excluded.
methodology.measurement_method: Binary self-deprecation flag + trigger + placement + function assigned per sampled response; counts tabulated programmatically; proportions extrapolated linearly to the full dataset. Sample counts/proportions tagged OBSERVED; full-dataset extrapolations tagged INFERRED.
methodology.limitations: Self-deprecation is a genuinely rare event in this sample (9 of 363, ~2.5%), so sub-category proportions (trigger, placement, function breakdowns) rest on a small base (n=9) and should be read as directional/HYPOTHESIS-adjacent rather than precise -- flagged explicitly below where relevant.

self_deprecation_frequency.note: Self-deprecation, strictly defined as an explicit self-critical reframe, is markedly less frequent than sarcasm in general (2.5% vs 59.2% of sampled responses) -- Chandler's default defense mechanism is sarcasm aimed outward/at situations, not inward at himself.

self_deprecation_intensity.description: All 9 observed instances were mild-to-moderate in intensity (light self-mockery embedded in a joke, never a sustained or severe self-attack); none rose to a 'strong' / distressed register.

triggers.note: No sampled instance followed direct praise of Chandler -- self-deprecation in this corpus is triggered far more often by awkward/embarrassing moments (56%) or arises unprompted as a spontaneous joke (33%) than as a reaction to being complimented or criticized.

placement_in_response.note: Because most Chandler responses are only 1-2 sentences (median response length in the full dataset is short), the self-deprecating beat typically IS the entire response ('whole', 78%) rather than being embedded as a discrete start/middle/end clause within a longer response; where the response is longer, the self-deprecating beat lands at the end (22%), functioning as a closing punchline/deflection rather than an opener.

secondary_function_avoid_vulnerability.description: 4 of 9 instances additionally serve to deflect an emotionally exposing topic (financial shame, cowardice, sex life, physical insecurity) -- the joke's real job is topic-avoidance, humor is the delivery mechanism.

soften_preceding_statement.description: No sampled instance used self-deprecation to soften a critical statement Chandler himself had just made about someone else; all instances were standalone jokes about himself, not face-saving hedges for a prior remark.

function.note: 100% of instances serve a humor function (self-deprecation is essentially always joke-packaged); within that, roughly 44% also do defensive work of avoiding a genuinely vulnerable topic.

emotional_context.finding: Self-deprecation instances skew toward serious/awkward preceding context (6 of 9, 67%) even though the overall sample is majority light-toned context (52%) -- self-deprecation, unlike sarcasm generally, appears disproportionately concentrated in moments of real or performed vulnerability rather than pure banter, consistent with a defense-mechanism reading.

structures.description: Abstract structural templates (setup -> mechanism -> outcome), no verbatim quotes.

templates.name: deflect_wellbeing_check
template: another character checks on speaker's emotional/physical state or asks a direct personal question
speaker deflects with a self-mocking admission of a personal flaw or bad decision
vulnerability is avoided and reframed as a joke

templates.name: embarrassing_evidence_reversal
template: speaker is confronted with unflattering evidence about himself (an old photo, a past dating habit)
speaker exaggerates or mock-panics about his own flaw rather than defending or explaining it
the embarrassment is neutralized through self-directed exaggeration

templates.name: criticism_deflection
template: another character relays criticism or a corrective note about speaker's behavior/performance
speaker responds with an unrelated, absurd self-deprecating aside about an unrelated trait (e.g. age)
the criticism is defused with humor rather than engaged with

templates.name: competitive_self_deprecation
template: another character claims a superlative bad/unlucky status for themselves
speaker outbids them by claiming an even worse version of the same trait for himself
self-deprecation becomes a bid for solidarity/attention rather than genuine distress

templates.name: avoidance_admission
template: speaker is placed in a situation requiring courage or direct confrontation
speaker explicitly admits he will avoid, hide from, or fail at it
the admission itself becomes the joke, defusing the tension without resolving it

templates.name: preemptive_self_mockery
template: speaker's competence, intelligence, or ability is implicitly relevant to the moment
speaker jokingly agrees with or exaggerates his own shortcoming before anyone else can
self-mockery preempts external criticism and closes off the topic

sarcasm_self_deprecation_cooccurrence.note: 8 of 9 self-deprecating instances (89%) are simultaneously sarcastic/ironic in delivery (deadpan, ironic statement, mock horror, exaggerated claim, self-mocking) -- self-deprecation is essentially a special case of sarcasm where the target happens to be the speaker himself, rather than a distinct sincere register.
